newsitem.title: USA: Calif. bill would place $1.25 bln bond on ballot.
newsitem.headline: Calif. bill would place $1.25 bln bond on ballot.

text.p: A California state assemblyman has introduced a bill that would place a $1.25 billion bond on the state ballot to fund projects at state colleges and universities, his office said Monday.
Introduced by Assemblyman Dennis Cardoza, a Democrat, Assembly Bill 1528 would enact the Higher Education Technology and Facilities Bond Act of June 1998.

If approval by the state's electorate, it would authorize the issuance of state general obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed $1.25 billion. The bond proceeds would fund improvements at state community colleges and universities.
The bill would place the bond measure on the June 2, 1998 ballot.
The bill is likely to be reviewed by the Assembly Higher Education Committee in early April, said Toni Symonds, Cardoza's spokeswoman.
